title: Relative Clauses (Nominative and Accusative)
summary: Connecting ideas and describing people or things with relative clauses.
whyItMatters: Relative clauses combine two sentences and add identifying information about a person or thing.

mentalModel.title: The noun gives gender and number
mentalModel.content: Choose der, die, das, or die from the noun being described.

mentalModel.title: The relative clause gives case
mentalModel.content: Use nominative when the pronoun performs the action and accusative when it receives the action.

ruleBlocks.title: Use nominative for the clause subject
ruleBlocks.content: Der Mann, der das Projekt leitet, ... has der as the actor.

ruleBlocks.title: Use accusative for the clause object
ruleBlocks.content: Das Fahrrad, das wir reparieren, ... has das as the object.

ruleBlocks.title: Put the finite verb at the end
ruleBlocks.content: Separate the relative clause with commas and move its finite verb to final position.

examples.de: Die Frau, die das Projekt organisiert, wohnt in unserer Straße.
examples.en: The woman who organizes the project lives on our street.

examples.de: Der Laden, den wir unterstützen, verkauft regionale Produkte.
examples.en: The shop that we support sells regional products.

examples.de: Das Gerät, das nicht mehr funktioniert, wird repariert.
examples.en: The device that no longer works is being repaired.

commonMistakes.reason: The pronoun is the subject, so nominative is required.

commonMistakes.wrong: Die Initiative, die wir unterstützen organisiert Kurse.
commonMistakes.correct: Die Initiative, die wir unterstützen, organisiert Kurse.
commonMistakes.reason: Both sides of the relative clause need commas.

comparisons.summary: Projects supply people and objects that need precise description.
Relative clauses help identify the exact proposal being discussed.
